summary.text: Alysia Regan is the Greens candidate for Euroa at the 2026 Victorian election. A mother of three, she works in the disability sector while studying health, and has earlier worked for government, including councils, in roles covering family services and emergency management. She was previously the Greens candidate for Sandringham at the 2022 state election and for Indi at the 2025 federal election.

prior_roles.role: Local government work (emergency management, family services)

priorities.text: Stronger public services and support for regional communities
Speaking up for children, young people with disability and their families as the NDIS changes

sources.title: Euroa: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Alysia Regan, Candidate for Euroa, Australian Greens Victoria

summary.text: Annabelle Cleeland has been the Nationals member for Euroa since the 2022 election, when she succeeded the retiring Steph Ryan. She was a national agricultural journalist with Fairfax and editor of Stock & Land, and since January 2025 she has been Shadow Assistant Minister for Health. She is recontesting Euroa in 2026.

prior_roles.role: Editor, Stock & Land; national agricultural journalist
Community adviser at her local hospital

priorities.text: Closing the gap in investment between regional Victoria and the city
Better access to quality health care
Better school results for regional children

summary.text: Karina Kelly is the Animal Justice Party candidate for Euroa at the 2026 Victorian election. She moved to Broadford about five years ago during the COVID-19 pandemic, working first at Kilmore Hospital and then at the Northern Hospital. She now works for a trade union representing healthcare workers.

priorities.text: A Kilmore high school, plus wider TAFE and university study options close to home
More frequent V/Line trains and buses with extra carriages at peak times
A new major hospital and specialist mental health care for the region
Tougher animal cruelty laws, a wildlife hospital and wildlife crossings on major roads

sources.title: Euroa: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Moussa Taouk is the Family First candidate for Euroa at the 2026 Victorian election. Born in Lebanon, he came to Australia at the age of eight and was brought up in a Catholic family. He is a mining engineer who studied at the University of New South Wales.

priorities.text: Making social and economic policy serve families, which he sees as the basis of a healthy society

summary.text: Steve Campbell is One Nation's candidate for Euroa at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC's guide says he was born in Warragul, worked as a tradesman in construction and later owned a building business, and is the historian for the Mansfield RSL. One Nation's candidate page could not be read by our scripts.

sources.title: Euroa: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Zoe Lyle is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Euroa at the 2026 Victorian election. She grew up in Shepparton, rents her home, and has been active in socialist organising for about five years. Her campaigning has included queer rights, refugee rights and school student strikes over Palestine.

priorities.text: Public, not-for-profit healthcare, transport, schools, aged care and disability support in regional towns
Stronger government action on climate change and better-funded emergency services

sources.title: Euroa: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
